items.title: Executable acceptance oracles are absent from the declared validation surfaces
items.statement: ATS-010 through ATS-013 describe rich behavioral suites, but the concrete validation surfaces in this core are plan and ledger validators, git diff checking, and multiple explicitly future suites. The core therefore cannot currently falsify incorrect runtime or GUI behavior, despite ATS-012 and ATS-013 explicitly rejecting validator-only evidence.
items.impact: A governance-green result can be mistaken for evidence that the specified workflows and failure cases execute correctly.

evidence.exact_quote: - python3 scripts/pm-plan-index.py validate
- Future DiscoveryService conformance suite.
- Do not treat validator success as evidence that user-facing History workflows were tested.
- Do not let validator success stand in for testing user-visible image bridge workflows.

items.title: Receipt producers, consumers, and authority are not assigned
items.statement: ATS-010 lists entities to which typed receipts are linked, but never identifies which component must emit each receipt, which callers may consume it, whether any receipt is mandatory, or which record is authoritative after duplicate delivery or restart.
items.impact: Implementations can produce incompatible or incomplete receipt graphs while still satisfying the prose.

items.impact: Execution can proceed on a stale or revoked capability while retaining a misleading successful preflight receipt.

items.title: Test mutation and cleanup lack authority, containment, and rollback contracts

items.impact: A test harness could modify protected project or remote state and fail to restore it without violating a measurable acceptance rule.

items.impact: Sensitive session and project data can become durable or broadly visible through otherwise conforming receipts.

items.impact: Upgrades can break audit chains or silently reinterpret historical execution evidence.

items.title: Discovery conformance explicitly tests policy non-leak and GUI truth
items.statement: ATS-011 closes several common negative spaces by requiring hidden and denied candidates not to leak through counts, ids, rank gaps, summaries, diagnostics, or receipts, while also covering GUI/agent parity and Assistant Chat visibility.

items.title: Discovery covers scheduler, cache migration, and resource-budget failure modes
items.statement: ATS-011 explicitly includes scheduler deduplication, cancellation and fairness, cache migration/rebuild/discard, remote freshness, timeouts, memory and disk budgets, and over-budget fallback receipts.

evidence.exact_quote: Automated_Testing_System owns validation for native DiscoveryService conformance, not service semantics. Tests cover ordinary no-exact-path bug-fix agent discovery, Builder orientation, Verifier exact-evidence follow-up, GUI/agent parity, every consumer conformance row, Assistant Chat discovery visibility on/off, SSH-backed discovery with no local checkout, remote/cache freshness, no local fallback, denied/hidden-by-policy no-leak behavior, root/home refusal, ignore and symlink policy, deterministic ranking, disabled/unsupported/backpressure/over-budget fallback receipts, frecency reset versus durable receipt retention, path identity versus display_path, cache migration/rebuild/discard behavior, scheduler dedupe/cancellation/fairness, and PlanUnit index discovery conformance without WorkNode creation.

- Performance budgets cover local warm query, GUI query, agent discover_paths, cold indexing, remote/SSH manifest query and refresh, watcher/reindex, cancellation, memory, disk, timeout, and over-budget fallback.

items.title: Discovery lacks a mid-operation network-loss oracle and measurable budget thresholds
items.statement: Remote/SSH freshness, no-local-fallback behavior, timeout, and over-budget fallback are named, but the core does not say what happens when connectivity drops during query, refresh, cancellation, or result delivery, and it provides no numeric thresholds or pass/fail measurement method for its performance budgets.
items.impact: Two implementations can expose different stale or partial results and incompatible latency/resource behavior while both claim conformance.

evidence.exact_quote: - Performance budgets cover local warm query, GUI query, agent discover_paths, cold indexing, remote/SSH manifest query and refresh, watcher/reindex, cancellation, memory, disk, timeout, and over-budget fallback.

items.title: Discovery GUI accessibility and localization are not tested
items.statement: ATS-011 declares GUI-facing scope and tests visibility, ranking, and degraded states, but no keyboard, focus, screen-reader, zoom, contrast, bidirectional text, localized search, collation, or path-display behavior is included.
items.impact: The same discovery state can be unusable or misleading for assistive-technology and non-English users while still passing the listed cases.

items.title: The every-consumer discovery seam has no locally defined completeness oracle
items.statement: ATS-011 requires every consumer row to have a scenario, but this core neither enumerates those rows nor binds a versioned manifest or completeness check. The dependency list and owner hints do not establish which consumers are required or how an added consumer makes the suite fail.
items.impact: A consumer can be omitted from conformance coverage without creating a deterministic failure in this contract.

evidence.exact_quote: - Each discovery consumer row has a validation scenario proving shared-substrate access and policy/freshness/fallback handling.

items.title: Untrusted image and OCR content is not adversarially tested
items.statement: The vision bridge accepts clipboard, OS screenshot, project-file, OCR, prompt, and provider output surfaces, but the core has no cases for malformed or oversized images, metadata leakage, decompression bombs, OCR or visual prompt injection, adversarial text embedded in an image, hostile provider output, or safe treatment of extracted instructions as untrusted data.

items.title: Vision consent, revocation, cache, and artifact lifecycle are not closed under races

items.impact: Revoked or differently scoped image data may remain usable, retry to another provider, or persist in cache and artifacts after the user believes access ended.

items.title: Operational correlation and support-safe diagnostics are not specified across suites
items.statement: The core mentions receipts, diagnostics, artifacts, and source lineage, but it provides no required correlation keys across user action, attempt, remote request, cache entry, export or rebuild; no support bundle contract; and no rule for balancing diagnostic usefulness with redaction and policy non-leak.
items.impact: Operators may be unable to reconstruct partial failures, while ad hoc diagnostics risk exposing the same protected data the tests intend to hide.

dimension_assessments.summary: Receipt producer/consumer ownership and the complete Discovery consumer set are not bound to enforceable manifests.
Preflight drift, History rebuild completion, and vision consent/cache transitions have unspecified intermediate and terminal states.
Duplicate/restart and scheduler cases are explicitly covered, but preflight TOCTOU, History rebuild/export races, and vision source/revocation races remain.
History partial export/rebuild and vision partial upload/output/reroute behavior lack pass/fail and cleanup rules.
Restart/cancellation fixtures exist, but mutation cleanup, History projection rollback, and export recovery are not defined.
Discovery policy and vision consent are named, but test mutation authority, History export authority, and revocation effects remain incomplete.
Policy non-leak and redaction are covered, while receipt retention, History export lifecycle, and vision cache/artifact deletion are unspecified.
The image/OCR/provider path has no malformed-input, resource-exhaustion, metadata, or visual prompt-injection cases.
Discovery parity and degraded states, History stale projection warnings, and vision fail-closed/stale/no-guessing states are explicitly tested.
Remote and provider-unavailable cases are named, but mid-operation disconnection, partial delivery, and reconnect behavior are not.
Discovery budget categories exist without thresholds, and History and vision lack large-dataset/image acceptance limits.
All three GUI-related PlanUnits omit concrete keyboard, focus, screen-reader, zoom, contrast, and reflow cases.
Localized search, path display, dates, sorting, bidi text, OCR, and consent/error messaging are absent.
Discovery cache migration is explicit, while typed receipts and vision providers/cache have no version evolution contract.
Receipts, diagnostics, artifacts, and lineage are named but lack cross-operation correlation and support-safe bundle rules.
No-build constraints are strong, but test mutation/cleanup and History rebuild lack containment, confirmation, and rollback acceptance rules.
Many dependency and owner references exist, but the Discovery every-consumer obligation is not locally enumerable or version-bound.
Behavioral claims are not connected to present executable test surfaces, expected outputs, or measurable oracles.
TOCTOU drift and adversarial image/OCR content expose unmodeled trust and timing failures beyond the enumerated happy/degraded matrices.
